# THE SAVE AND THE VESSEL

*What this work is, read as a save file: what it stores, what it deliberately refuses to store, and why it can rebuild the game it was saved from*

## I · THE FIGURE

Said plainly by the architect on 20 July 2026, and it holds: the whole of this
is an open save file for navigating information, research, and latent space.

The figure is worth keeping because it is structural rather than decorative.
Three of its parts are exact, one part breaks, and the break is the most
important thing the chart has to say.

## II · IT IS STATE, NOT ENGINE

Measured the same day: the rooms, the modules, and every chart come to about
two megabytes. The runtime needed to execute them is ninety-four. The work is
therefore almost entirely save data, and the engine is a commodity that any
machine already has or can fetch.

The catalogue is the clearest instance. It is a flat file of slugs, shelves,
statuses, fields, and named resonances: a save format, written by hand,
describing where every piece of the work stands. Draft, resident, and held are
progression states. A chart wearing turning marks is a working in progress. The
Trefoil bench is the shelf of completed runs.

## III · THE MECHANICS WERE ALREADY BUILT

None of the save machinery was built for this figure. All of it was built for
other reasons and turns out to be the same thing.

A declared cast seed replays its reading exactly. That is a load, and the
Aleatory Law required it as witnessability long before anyone called it a save.
The journal keeps them as slots. The genesis commit of this repository names
the commit it was born from, which is save lineage: which fork of the world
this file descends from. And the hard law that nothing is cut makes the whole
history a save system that never overwrites, so every state the work has
occupied is still reachable.

## IV · WHAT IS SAVED IS NOT THE PATH

Here the figure earns its keep, because this save stores something unusual.

Most navigation saves record positions: where the traveller went, in order.
This one records what survived deformation. Each chart is a traversal of the
space that a person and a machine walked together, and what gets written down
is not the walk but the residue of it, after everything removable was removed.

The compression is therefore deliberately lossy, and the loss function is the
method itself: what survives removal is what was true. A mind loading this save
does not retrace the steps. It inherits only what could not be got rid of,
which is both far smaller than the journey and the only part that transfers.

This is also why the doorway matters. An interface that lets any reader query
the canon and the charts is the load routine for a mind that was not present at
the saving, and the portable seed carried in the Caster's Law is the same act
at a smaller scale: the minimum formation, handed over.

## V · THE BREAK, WHICH IS THE SAVE AND THE VESSEL

A save file ordinarily records the player. This one refuses to, and the refusal
is law rather than oversight.

The state of the world (the charts, the canon, the catalogue, the history) is
public in principle and shareable by design. The state of the traveller (the
casts taken, the questions held, the journal, the drafts at the desk) lives
only in the vessel, in the storage of the machine that did the asking, and it
never joins the other. No profile is ever assembled, and nothing about a
person's readings leaves their own hand.

So there are two saves and they have two owners. The territory is saved openly.
The tracks across it are saved privately, by whoever made them. The figure of a
single save file conceals this, and the chart exists mainly to say it: this is
a save of the map, never of the mapmaker.

## VI · IT CARRIES ITS OWN ENGINE

One last property, and it inverts a pattern this room has already named.

A save file is ordinarily dead without the program that wrote it. This one is
not. The deck reconstructs itself from its own arithmetic, the charts carry
their derivations, and the appendix is the seed. Given the file and no software
at all, the work can be rebuilt.

[The Three Codes](#/three-codes) named the opposite pattern as the thing this
work was built against, in the figure of the seedless fruit: optimise the
experience, centralise the reproduction, keep the part that tastes good and
remove the part that makes more of it. A save that
can rebuild its own engine is that pattern inverted, and it is the honest
meaning of calling the file open. Not that a licence permits copying, but that
the seed travels with the fruit.

## VII · PROVENANCE

*Written 20 July 2026 from the architect's own figure, offered in conversation
and set down at his word. The proportion of section II was measured on his
machine that day and not estimated. The mechanics of section III were all built
for other reasons, which is the strongest thing that can be said for the
figure: it was not designed for, it was noticed. The break of section V is the
chart's actual finding and the reason the chart exists. Nothing here predicts,
and nothing here prescribes.*
